name: Assess and treat inpatients referred to allied health
summary: Physiotherapists, occupational therapists, social workers, dietitians and speech-language pathologists receive referrals for inpatients through the electronic record, rank them by discharge urgency, assess the patient at the bedside and write recommendations that decide whether the patient can go home safely. Therapy assistants and therapists then give follow-up sessions until discharge, and dietitians and speech-language pathologists change diet orders. Cover is thin on weekends and holidays, so Friday referrals wait, and a therapy assessment that is late can hold up a discharge or send a patient home without the equipment or help they need.

baseline.org_archetype: A three-site Ontario community hospital corporation with about 640 beds and a centrally managed allied health department deployed by unit.
baseline.notes: Social work time spent on discharge planning itself is counted in hosp-cs-discharge-planning; only other psychosocial referrals are counted here. Respiratory therapy works from orders and is not included.

unit_of_work: one allied health referral (one discipline, one patient stay)
trigger: A physician or nurse enters an allied health referral order for an inpatient.
end_state: The patient has been assessed, recommendations are in the chart and passed to the team, follow-up treatment has ended at discharge, and any diet order change is in place; or the patient left before being seen.

volume.seasonality: Follows medicine admissions, higher in January to March; surgical referrals dropped during the 2020 and 2021 pauses in scheduled surgery.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate kept: about two to three referrals per inpatient stay across five disciplines.
Author's estimate tied to winter medicine admission peaks.

Enters therapy and dietitian referrals; nurses enter many under medical directives (for example, a positive nutrition or swallowing screen). Author's estimate. Loaded costs are the organisation file's ranges: hourly wage x 1.35 (about 25% benefits and HOOPP pension plus 10% overhead). Physician costs are gross clinical earnings paid by the province, not hospital payroll. Roles added here use the same 1.35 factor.
Builds the weekend priority list and moves staff between units when backlogs build. Author's estimate.
Physiotherapists are part of the inpatient multidisciplinary team (oag2010) and the core stroke team (stroke_bp). FTE is the author's estimate of the inpatient share of 55 physiotherapists.

roles.title: Rehabilitation assistant (physiotherapy and occupational therapy assistant)

evidence.note: Ontario hospitals commonly use PT/OT assistants for follow-up mobility sessions; not in the organisation file. Loaded cost uses the 1.35 factor on an author-estimated wage. Headcount 10 to 15 at three sites.
Occupational therapists are part of the core interdisciplinary team (stroke_bp). FTE is the author's estimate of the inpatient share of 35 OTs.
Social workers are on the multidisciplinary team (oag2010). Only non-discharge psychosocial referrals are counted here. Author's FTE estimate.
Dietitians are part of the core interdisciplinary team (stroke_bp). FTE is the author's estimate of the inpatient share of 20 dietitians.
Speech-language pathologists assess swallowing and communication (stroke_bp). FTE is the author's estimate of the inpatient share of 8 SLPs.

systems.name: Hospital information system (electronic patient record with ADT, order entry, results, eMAR and clinical documentation)
Email, telephone, pagers and wireless phones
Radiology information system, PACS and voice recognition dictation

steps.name: Enter the allied health referral
steps.description: The hospitalist, or a nurse under a medical directive, enters a referral order in the electronic record naming the discipline, the reason (mobility, function, swallowing, nutrition, psychosocial) and any urgency, often linked to the estimated discharge date.

error.defect_description: Vague reason for referral, so the therapist must phone the unit

evidence.note: Author's estimate; referral by order entry or medical directive is common Ontario practice.

steps.name: Route the referral to the discipline worklist
steps.description: The electronic record places the order on the discipline's worklist for the patient's unit and prints a requisition in the department; referrals entered after mid-afternoon on Friday land on the weekend list.

next.condition: arrives Friday afternoon, weekend or holiday

evidence.note: Discipline mix is the author's estimate; about one referral in five arrives when only reduced weekend cover is on.

steps.name: Build the weekend priority list
steps.description: On Friday afternoon the allied health manager or lead therapist reviews pending referrals and builds the weekend list: patients due to go home, new stroke or hip fracture admissions and swallowing screens are seen; the rest wait for Monday.

evidence.note: Fewer staff work weekends and discharges fall 25% (oag2016). The priority list practice is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review and prioritise the physiotherapy referral
steps.description: The physiotherapy clinician covering the unit opens the referral on the department worklist, reads the admission notes, orders, precautions and estimated discharge date, and ranks it: discharge-critical and new admissions first, routine follow-ups later in the day or the next day.

error.defect_description: Discharge-critical referral ranked as routine and seen after the planned discharge date

next.condition: patient discharged or transferred before being seen

evidence.note: Physiotherapists work extended hours with thin weekend cover; the weekend gap is in oag2016. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Assess mobility at the bedside
steps.description: The physiotherapist assesses strength, balance, transfers, walking and stairs, checks oxygen and pain, decides what aid and supervision the patient needs and whether the patient is safe to go home or needs rehabilitation.

evidence.note: Interdisciplinary assessment ideally within 48 hours of admission (stroke_bp). Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Document mobility recommendations
steps.description: The physiotherapist writes the assessment and discharge recommendation in the chart (home, home with aid, home with home care physiotherapy, or rehabilitation), updates the whiteboard and tells the charge nurse or coordinator.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Give follow-up mobility sessions
steps.description: A rehabilitation assistant walks and exercises the patient once or twice a day following the physiotherapist's plan, and reports progress or problems back. Minutes add up the sessions until discharge.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Review and prioritise the occupational therapy referral
steps.description: The occupational therapy clinician covering the unit opens the referral on the department worklist, reads the admission notes, orders, precautions and estimated discharge date, and ranks it: discharge-critical and new admissions first, routine follow-ups later in the day or the next day.

error.defect_description: Discharge-critical referral ranked as routine and seen after the planned discharge date

next.condition: patient discharged or transferred before being seen

evidence.note: Occupational therapists work extended hours with thin weekend cover; the weekend gap is in oag2016. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Assess function and cognition
steps.description: The occupational therapist assesses self-care (dressing, toileting, bathing), cognition and safety, and asks about the home layout to judge whether the patient can manage at home and what equipment or help is needed.

evidence.note: Assessment ideally within 48 hours of admission (stroke_bp). Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Recommend equipment and supports
steps.description: The occupational therapist documents the assessment and recommends equipment (raised toilet seat, bath bench, walker), home care personal support or a home safety visit, and passes the list to the patient care coordinator.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Give follow-up function sessions
steps.description: The occupational therapist practises transfers, dressing and memory strategies with the patient, trains the family on equipment, and updates the recommendation before discharge. Minutes add up the sessions.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Review and prioritise the social work referral
steps.description: The social work clinician covering the unit opens the referral on the department worklist, reads the admission notes, orders, precautions and estimated discharge date, and ranks it: discharge-critical and new admissions first, routine follow-ups later in the day or the next day.

error.defect_description: Discharge-critical referral ranked as routine and seen after the planned discharge date

next.condition: patient discharged or transferred before being seen

evidence.note: Social workers work weekday office hours, so weekend referrals wait for Monday (oag2016 describes thin weekend staffing). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Assess and counsel the patient and family
steps.description: The social worker meets the patient and family about the concern raised (coping, caregiver strain, finances or drug coverage, substitute decision-making, suspected abuse) and gives counselling or connects them to services.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Document the psychosocial plan
steps.description: The social worker writes the assessment and plan in the chart, makes any outside referrals by phone or fax, and flags issues that affect the discharge date to the team.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Review and prioritise the dietitian referral
steps.description: The dietitian clinician covering the unit opens the referral on the department worklist, reads the admission notes, orders, precautions and estimated discharge date, and ranks it: discharge-critical and new admissions first, routine follow-ups later in the day or the next day.

error.defect_description: Discharge-critical referral ranked as routine and seen after the planned discharge date

next.condition: patient discharged or transferred before being seen

evidence.note: Dietitians work weekday office hours; weekend referrals wait (oag2016 describes thin weekend staffing). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Assess nutrition
steps.description: The dietitian reviews weight history, intake records, labs and swallowing status, interviews the patient, and estimates energy and protein needs for malnutrition, diabetes, renal or tube-feeding problems.

evidence.note: Dietitians are on the core team and patients are assessed for dysphagia and nutrition (stroke_bp). Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Document the nutrition plan
steps.description: The dietitian writes the nutrition care plan and teaching in the chart and decides whether the diet order, supplements or tube feed need to change.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Enter the diet order change
steps.description: The dietitian enters the new diet, supplement or tube-feed order in the electronic record under a medical directive, which sends it to the diet office for the next meal tray.

error.defect_description: Wrong texture or supplement code reaches the diet office

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Review and prioritise the speech-language pathology referral
steps.description: The speech-language pathology clinician covering the unit opens the referral on the department worklist, reads the admission notes, orders, precautions and estimated discharge date, and ranks it: discharge-critical and new admissions first, routine follow-ups later in the day or the next day.

error.defect_description: Discharge-critical referral ranked as routine and seen after the planned discharge date

next.condition: patient discharged or transferred before being seen

evidence.note: Speech-language pathologists work weekdays; urgent swallowing referrals go on the weekend list. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Assess swallowing at the bedside
steps.description: The speech-language pathologist examines oral and throat function and watches the patient swallow different textures and liquids to judge aspiration risk, and assesses speech and language when asked.

control.basis: Hospital dysphagia policy: patients who fail a swallowing screen stay nil by mouth until assessed

evidence.note: Patients are assessed for dysphagia by the interdisciplinary team (stroke_bp). Minutes and share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Book and attend a videofluoroscopic swallow study
steps.description: The speech-language pathologist requests a modified barium swallow from diagnostic imaging, waits for a fluoroscopy slot and porter, runs the study with the radiologist or technologist and reviews the images in PACS.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; fluoroscopy slots for swallow studies are usually booked a few days ahead.

steps.name: Set the diet texture and document
steps.description: The speech-language pathologist writes the recommendation (texture, liquid thickness, positioning, supervision), enters the diet texture order and posts swallowing precautions at the bedside.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Weekend referral wait
exceptions.description: A referral entered on Friday afternoon is not discharge-critical, so it waits until Monday; if the physician is ready to discharge on the weekend, the patient waits for the assessment.

exceptions.name: Discharged before being seen
exceptions.description: The patient goes home or is transferred before the therapist reaches them, sometimes without the equipment or home care the therapist would have recommended.

exceptions.name: Instrumental swallow study
exceptions.description: The bedside swallowing assessment is inconclusive and the patient waits days on a modified diet or nil by mouth for a fluoroscopy slot.

benchmarks.unit: days from referral to end of allied health involvement
benchmarks.population: inpatient allied health referrals in an Ontario community hospital

evidence.note: Author's estimate: first visit same or next weekday, follow-up until a median acute stay of about four days ends.
The interdisciplinary team should assess all patients as soon as possible after admission, ideally within 48 hours.

benchmarks.unit: share fewer daily discharges on weekends

evidence.note: Attributed to fewer physicians and support staff on weekends.

pain_points.description: Thin weekend and holiday cover means non-urgent referrals wait until Monday and can delay discharges.

evidence.note: oag2016 links 25% fewer weekend discharges to fewer staff on duty; the referral wait is the author's inference.

pain_points.description: Referrals with vague reasons or sent late in the stay leave too little time to assess and arrange equipment before discharge.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Recommendations sit in the chart until the next bullet round, so discharge plans change late.

evidence.note: Bullet rounds often had little input from disciplines other than nursing (oag2010).

sources.title: Canadian Stroke Best Practice Recommendations: Acute Stroke Management, Section 8, Acute Stroke Unit Care (2022 update)
sources.publisher: Heart and Stroke Foundation of Canada
sources.supports: Core interdisciplinary team (OT, PT, SLP, social work, dietitian); assessment ideally within 48 hours; dysphagia, mood and cognition assessment; post-acute rehabilitation needs within 72 hours.

sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario
sources.supports: Fewer staff and 25% fewer discharges on weekends.

sources.title: 2010 Annual Report, Chapter 3, Section 3.02: Discharge of Hospital Patients
sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario

assumptions: One case is one discipline's referral for one stay, including all follow-up visits; a patient seen by PT and OT is two cases.
Rehabilitation assistants (PT/OT assistants) are not in the organisation file but deliver most follow-up mobility sessions in Ontario hospitals; they are added with not_in_org_file.

Discipline mix (PT 36%, OT 22%, dietitian 22%, social work 10%, SLP 10%) is the author's estimate; social work referrals for discharge planning are counted in the discharge-planning workflow, not here.
Weekend and holiday cover is modelled as a 20% share of referrals routed through the weekend priority list, with longer waits in the review steps.
The imaging order for swallow studies goes to diagnostic imaging booking; the organisation file does not link this process to imaging.

Loaded costs are the organisation file's ranges: hourly wage x 1.35 (about 25% benefits and HOOPP pension plus 10% overhead). Physician costs are gross clinical earnings paid by the province, not hospital payroll. Roles added here use the same 1.35 factor.
